To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a neural network that performs reflectance decomposition, and that we propose a novel illumination integration method.
we propose a novel reflectances decomposition network that can accurately estimate shape, BRDT, and per-image lighting given a set of images captured under varying lighting.
we propose a neural reflectance decomposition network called Neural-Pil that uses a novel neural illumination integration network to estimate shape, BRDf, and illumination from images.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: 1. How can we decompose the scene into shape, reflectance, and illumination? 2. How can we accurately recover the illumination? 3. Can we use neural networks to solve these problems?

1) How to decompose an image into its reflectance and illumination components, 2) How to represent the illumination and BRDF components in a low dimensional space, and 3) How to perform the rendering of a scene given the decomposed components.
- Learning a neural network that can decompose a scene into its reflectance and illumination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is a new approach to reflectance decomposition, which is a key step in many computer graphics applications.
we propose a novel neural reflectance decomposition network for shape, BRDF and per-image illumination estimation that outperforms prior art in novel view synthesis and relighting.

Neural-PIL is a novel reflectance and lighting decomposition network that uses a novel illumination integration neural network to estimate shape, BRDIF, and per-image lighting given a set of images of an object under varying illumination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel illumination decomposition network that can decompose an object into its shape, BRDF and illumination.
we have proposed a neural network that can decompose an image into its shape, surface properties and illumination.

we have proposed an end-to-end deep learning framework for decomposing a set of images of a static object captured under varying illumination conditions into a shape, a BRDF (reflectance) model, and per-image light.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can learn an accurate reflectance decomposition network by integrating a novel illumination integration module, which replaces a costly illumination integration operation in the rendering equation with a simple network.
we can learn a neural representation of lighting and BRDFs in a way that enables more accurate novel view synthesis and relighting compared with prior work.
we show how to perform reflectance decomposition using a single network.
